walkthroughs.body_html:
Just war began with Augustine and Aquinas.

Going to war (jus ad bellum): just cause, last resort, legitimate authority, proportionate, reasonable chance of success.

Conduct in war (jus in bello): discrimination (only combatants targeted) and proportionality (no excessive force).

Holy war = war fought for religious reasons.

Christian example: the Crusades (1095 onwards) — Pope Urban II called them. Modern Christianity rejects holy war.

Islam's jihad is often mistranslated. Greater jihad = inner struggle; lesser jihad = outer struggle, only defensive, with strict rules (no harming civilians, women, children).

Pacifism: violence is always wrong. Jesus said 'turn the other cheek' (Matthew 5:39) and 'love your enemies' (5:44).

The Quakers have refused to fight since 1660. In WW1 many were imprisoned as conscientious objectors.

Dietrich Bonhoeffer was a Lutheran pacifist who later joined the plot to assassinate Hitler — showing pacifism can be tested by extreme evil. He was executed in 1945.
